title: Benchmark Lab Expansion Foundation
goal: Expand AegisPT's safe target catalog and acceptance harness so product validation is not limited to a handful of web and API labs.
scope: Extend the repo-owned benchmark catalog and acceptance harness to support a broader and more truthful benchmark set. The first expansion slice should add catalog structure, fixture notes, and safe-scenario support for: OWASP Benchmark, WrongSecrets, PromptMe, and an internal-lab template for GOAD-style AD validation, plus richer metadata for Gruyere, Juice Shop, WebGoat, crAPI, and PortSwigger Web Security Academy references. Where a target can run locally and safely, add executable catalog entries and scenario stubs. Where a benchmark is documentation-only or hosted, add explicit documentation metadata, expected vulnerable-family coverage, and prerequisites rather than pretending it is automatically runnable.
generation_reason: The audit found that the current safe target catalog is too narrow for the breadth of runtimes now present in the repo. Internal AD, secrets, LLM, and benchmark-score truth are still underrepresented in practical product validation.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement this task until it is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Catalog and harness expansion only. Do not silently enable public or unauthorized targets. Every executable target must remain local, explicitly authorized, or deliberately vulnerable.
notes: This task expands benchmark truth; it does not replace backlog-99 validation scoring.
Documentation-only benchmarks must stay explicitly marked as non-runnable when appropriate.

success_criteria: The benchmark catalog covers more than the current local-smoke/Juice-Shop/WebGoat/crAPI set.
New benchmark metadata explicitly records vuln families, prerequisites, and whether the target is runnable, fixture-backed, or documentation-only.
At least one non-web benchmark family is represented in the catalog.
Tests cover catalog parsing, unsupported-target handling, and fixture metadata truth.
No unauthorized or arbitrary public target execution is introduced.

acceptance_criteria: Expanded benchmark catalog remains safe and explicit.
Documentation-only versus runnable targets are distinguished clearly.
No unauthorized targets are enabled by default.

before_promotion: The prior active task is completed and logged.
Benchmark target safety rules are documented.
after_completion: Update DONE_LOG.md with benchmark catalog expansion and validation evidence.
Update CURRENT_STATE.md with expanded benchmark-truth coverage.
Promote exactly one next approved task package into NEXT_TASK.md, or set an explicit holding state if the queue is exhausted.
